title: Aan de telefoon
subtitle: Phone calls
intro: After this lesson you can make and answer phone calls in Dutch. You will learn how to say who you are, ask for someone, ask people to repeat or speak more slowly, and spell your name. You can also move or cancel an appointment by phone.

grammar.title: Aan de telefoon: de juiste frasen
grammar.explanation: You answer the phone with **Met** + your name. **Met Sara.** is short for **U spreekt met Sara.** and means 'Sara speaking'. In a formal call you can say **U spreekt met ...**. To ask for someone, use **Kan ik ... spreken?** The assistant says **Ik verbind u door** when she connects you.

rows: Kan ik meneer De Vries spreken?

examples.en: Can I speak to the assistant?

grammar.tip: Don't say **Ik ben Sara** when you answer the phone; say **Met Sara**.

grammar.title: Kunt u dat herhalen?
grammar.explanation: If you don't understand, ask **Kunt u dat herhalen?** To ask for slower speech, use **Kunt u wat langzamer praten?** **Kunt u** is the polite form with **u**; the verb comes first. **Wat** softens the request: 'a little'.

examples.nl: Kunt u dat herhalen? Ik begrijp het niet.
examples.en: Can you repeat that? I don't understand.
Can you speak a little more slowly?

grammar.tip: **Langzamer** is the comparative of **langzaam**; use it when someone speaks too fast.

grammar.title: Spellen: het alfabet
grammar.explanation: When you spell a name, say each letter separately. Some Dutch letter names are different from English: **ij** is *ei*, **g** is *gee* (with a Dutch g), **j** is *jee* ('yay'). Ask **Hoe spelt u dat?** and spell slowly.

examples.en: How do you spell your surname?

grammar.tip: Say **ij** as **ei**, not as two letters.

dialogue.title: Bij de tandartspraktijk
dialogue.setting: You call the dentist's practice to move your appointment; the assistant answers.

lines.speaker: Assistente
lines.en: De Molen dental practice, good morning.

lines.speaker: Meneer Bakker
lines.nl: Goedemorgen, u spreekt met Adam Bakker.

lines.nl: Goedemorgen, meneer Bakker. Wat kan ik voor u doen?
lines.en: Good morning, Mr Bakker. How can I help you?

lines.nl: Ik heb een afspraak op maandag, maar ik kan niet komen. Kan ik de afspraak verzetten?
lines.en: I have an appointment on Monday, but I can't come. Can I move the appointment?

lines.nl: Natuurlijk. Een momentje, alstublieft. ... Wanneer wilt u komen?

lines.speaker: Assistente

lines.en: Thursday at three is still free.

lines.speaker: Meneer Bakker
lines.nl: Dat is goed. Kunt u dat bevestigen?
lines.en: That's good. Can you confirm that?

lines.speaker: Assistente
lines.nl: Ja, ik stuur u een e-mail. Hoe spelt u uw achternaam?
lines.en: Yes, I'll send you an email. How do you spell your surname?

lines.speaker: Assistente
lines.nl: Dank u wel. En uw telefoonnummer?
lines.en: Thank you. And your phone number?

lines.speaker: Meneer Bakker
lines.nl: Dat is nul zes, een twee drie vier vijf zes zeven acht.

lines.speaker: Assistente
lines.nl: Dank u. Ik stuur u vandaag een e-mail. Tot donderdag!
lines.en: Thank you. I'll send you an email today. See you Thursday!

lines.speaker: Meneer Bakker
lines.nl: Tot donderdag. Dank u wel. Doei.
lines.en: See you Thursday. Thank you. Bye.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'ik ben + name' instead of 'met + name' (e.g. 'Hallo, ik ben Sara.')
mistakes.explain: On the phone say **Met Sara**, not **Ik ben Sara**.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'name + spreekt' alone (e.g. 'Hallo, Sara spreekt.')
mistakes.explain: Say **Met Sara** or **U spreekt met Sara**, not **Sara spreekt**.

mistakes.pattern: Omits 'met' before the name (e.g. 'Hallo, Sara.')
mistakes.explain: Add **met**: **Hallo, met Sara.**

mistakes.pattern: Adds extra 'spreekt' after 'met + name' (e.g. 'Hallo, met Sara spreekt.')
mistakes.explain: Keep it short: **Hallo, met Sara.**

mistakes.pattern: Keeps the subject before the verb in a yes/no question (e.g. 'Ik kan de dokter spreken?')
mistakes.explain: Start with the verb: **Kan ik de dokter spreken?**

mistakes.pattern: Puts the infinitive before the object (e.g. 'Kan ik spreken de dokter?')
mistakes.explain: The infinitive goes at the end: **Kan ik de dokter spreken?**

mistakes.pattern: Omits the verb 'spreken' (e.g. 'Kan ik de dokter?')

mistakes.pattern: Uses positive 'langzaam' instead of comparative 'langzamer' for 'more slowly' (e.g. 'Kunt u langzaam praten?')
mistakes.explain: Use the comparative **langzamer**: **Kunt u wat langzamer praten?**

mistakes.pattern: Puts the infinitive before the adverb (e.g. 'Kunt u praten langzamer?')
mistakes.explain: The infinitive goes at the end: **Kunt u langzamer praten?**

mistakes.pattern: Keeps the subject before the verb in a question (e.g. 'U kunt langzamer praten?')

mistakes.pattern: Omits the verb 'praten' (e.g. 'Kunt u langzamer?')
mistakes.explain: Add **praten**: **Kunt u langzamer praten?**

mistakes.pattern: Keeps the separable prefix with the verb (e.g. 'Ik terugbel u morgen.')
mistakes.explain: Split the separable verb: **Ik bel u morgen terug.**

mistakes.pattern: Uses the infinitive after a finite verb without a modal (e.g. 'Ik bel u morgen terugbellen.')
mistakes.explain: Use the finite verb and split the prefix: **Ik bel u morgen terug.**

mistakes.pattern: Places 'morgen' after the prefix 'terug' (e.g. 'Ik bel u terug morgen.')

mistakes.pattern: Puts the object after the prefix (e.g. 'Ik bel morgen terug u.')
mistakes.explain: Put the object before the time and prefix: **Ik bel u morgen terug.**

culture.title: Met Jansen: je naam zeggen aan de telefoon
culture.text: In the Netherlands people usually answer the phone with their name rather than just 'hallo': **Met Jansen** or **Met Sara**. This is normal and considered polite, even when you don't know who is calling. In formal calls you may hear **U spreekt met ...**; the same phrase is used when you call someone and give your name. So don't wait for the other person to ask who you are.

summary: Answer the phone with **Met** + your name: **Met Sara.**
Use **Kan ik ... spreken?** to ask for someone and **Ik verbind u door** to connect.
Ask **Kunt u dat herhalen?** or **Kunt u wat langzamer praten?** when you don't understand.
Spell names letter by letter; **ij** is **ei**, **g** is **gee**, **j** is **jee**.
